title: Parse a time of day into minutes
prompt:
Shift times come in from a form as text and we need them as minutes after midnight. Add an exported parseClock(input: string): number to src/clock.ts (next to formatClock) that accepts both of these forms, ignoring surrounding whitespace:

- 24-hour: H:MM or HH:MM, hours 0-23, for example "19:30" -> 1170 and "7:05" -> 425.
- 12-hour: an hour of 1-12, optionally followed by :MM, then am or pm in any letter case, with or without a space before it: "7:30 pm" -> 1170, "7pm" -> 1140, "9 Am" -> 540. 12am is midnight ("12:15 am" -> 15) and 12pm is noon ("12pm" -> 720).

The hour is one or two digits and minutes, when present, are always exactly two digits (00-59). A bare hour with no minutes and no am/pm, such as "7", is not accepted.

Errors: throw a RangeError when the text has the right shape but a number is out of range ("24:00", "7:60", "13pm", "0am"), and a SyntaxError for anything else that doesn't match either form ("", "7", "7:5", "noon", "7:30 p.m.").
acceptance: 24-hour and 12-hour forms with the prompt's examples, 12am/12pm, case-insensitive am/pm, whitespace trimming, RangeError for out-of-range hours and minutes in both forms, SyntaxError for malformed strings.
difficulty_rationale: One function; the 12am/12pm rule and the RangeError/SyntaxError split are the only edge cases.
